# HLT-C5 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Raine R, Wallace I, Nic a' Bháird C, et al. (2014). Improving the effectiveness of multidisciplinary team meetings for patients with chronic diseases: a prospective observational study. Health Services and Delivery Research 2(37). doi:10.3310/hsdr02370.

Text: supplied PDF (208 pages), converted with pdftotext -layout to _text/full.txt. Page references use the printed report pagination (roman numerals for front matter; arabic page n = PDF page n + 34).

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- Object: weekly multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings of 12 NHS chronic disease teams (cancer, heart failure, memory clinic, community mental health) in North Thames (p.xxv; p.9).
- Relationships studied: among professionals in the team (skill mix, team climate, hierarchy, chairing; p.41-43, p.49-52) and between team and patient (patient awareness, attendance, feedback, preferences; p.61-66).
- Public service: MDT meetings are "endorsed by the Department of Health as the core model for managing chronic diseases" (abstract, p.vii); permissions obtained "at each of the NHS organisations that participated in the study" (p.9); funded by NIHR HS&DR (p.viii).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: random-effects logistic regression of treatment plan implementation on 2512 patients (Table 9, p.28); Team Climate Inventory from 161 members (p.23); expert panel ratings with medians and MADM (p.80-82).
- Qualitative: thematic analysis of observation of 370 meetings, 53 professional and 20 patient interviews (Chapter 4, p.33-67); thematic analysis of the consensus meeting transcript (p.79-83).

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
